title: Nvidia Launches Isaac OS to Power General Purpose AI Robots
summary:
A new collection of AI training tools and physics-based simulators was unveiled at GTC Berlin to help developers deploy complex autonomous machinery. Nvidia's expansion of the Isaac platform includes Isaac OS, a new open-source runtime for real-time operations, and Isaac Lab 3.0 for refining robot behaviors. The company also released the Human 1M Dataset, consisting of 3D hand-tracking data and human activity videos, along with more than 2,000 simulation-ready factory and robotics assets.

Agile Robots debuted the Agile ONE SN, a reference humanoid powered by the Jetson Thor processor and Isaac GR00T, which is scheduled for release in early 2027. Industrial partners including ABB Robotics, KUKA, and Universal Robots are adopting the technologies as the industry seeks a "ChatGPT moment" for robotics. To further development, Nvidia added three open-source workflows to its DGX Station for optimizing GR00T models via reinforcement learning and synthetic data generation.

selectedTweets.text:
$NVDA ANNOUNCES MAJOR EXPANSION OF ITS ISAAC ROBOTICS PLATFORM, INCLUDING A NEW HUMANOID ROBOT

“the ChatGPT moment for robotics is fast approaching.”

At GTC Berlin, NVIDIA introduced new humanoid robotics technology, AI training tools, simulation datasets, and software designed to accelerate the development of general-purpose robots.

Here's what's new:

• Agile ONE SN: A new humanoid reference robot developed by Agile Robots, powered by NVIDIA Jetson Thor and Isaac GR00T. It stands 1.4 meters tall, weighs 40 kg, features 31 degrees of freedom, and has two five-finger hands. Expected in early 2027.

• Isaac Lab 3.0: Now generally available, enabling developers to train and refine robot behaviors using multi-GPU workflows and physics-based simulation.

• Isaac OS: A new open-source runtime connecting AI models, sensors, controls, and robot hardware for real-time operation.

• New Training Data: More than 2,000 simulation-ready robotics and factory assets, alongside the Human 1M Dataset containing human activity videos and 3D hand-tracking data.

• DGX Station: Three new open-source workflows for improving GR00T models through reinforcement learning, developing complex manipulation skills, and generating synthetic training data using NVIDIA Cosmos.

Companies including ABB Robotics, KUKA, NEURA Robotics, Universal Robots, Hexagon Robotics, Humanoid, and Sereact are building on NVIDIA's technologies for industrial robotics applications.
